runs.name: Run 10
runs.title: All-native + degradation loss 0.1
runs.summary: Run 8 plus a contrastive degradation loss. Each HR crop is generated with four references from the batch (same noise); for each reference, DEResNet must pick the output it produced. Near-identical references share the target.
runs.purpose: In Runs 7–9 the outputs did not follow their reference. With identical content in all four outputs, only the degradation can decide which output belongs to which reference.
variables: soft-target InfoNCE, weight 0.1, τ 0.1, τ_t 0.05, K 4, from 10k steps (1k ramp)
findings: Outputs follow their reference: own reference ranked closest 54% of the time (chance 25%).
Costs about 4 FID points against Run 8.

In the native sweep the Canon reference makes grass and edges clearly more contrasty, and the striped-facade reference (panasonic_187) puts a faint repeating pattern on a flat wall: reference texture leaks into the native LR.
runs.verdict: The loss works, at a quality cost.

runs.name: Run 18

runs.summary: As Run 14, but each output must also be farther from the DEResNet embedding of the reference's clean HR (area-downscaled to native) than from its reference LR. The HR negative is weighted by 1 − cos(ref LR, ref HR) / 0.1, so it is off for near-clean references.

runs.name: Run 20
runs.title: Run 14 with the degradation direction as the target (delta target)

runs.verdict: Best trade-off so far: Run 12-level reference following without its leak. Candidate base for the next runs.

runs.name: Run 24
runs.title: Run 20 + synthetic same-content pairs in the reconstruction losses
runs.summary: As Run 20, plus synthetic pairs: each step 4 HRs x 4 known degradations (anisotropic blur, x4 area, noise, JPEG; blur range matched to DRealSR). The reference is the degradation applied to another HR, the target the same degradation applied to the input HR; the native losses (low-pass MSE, LPIPS, PSD) are applied against it. The discriminator sees real batches only.
runs.purpose: Teach reference following with an exact target: only applying the reference's degradation to the input reaches it, and copying the reference's content raises the loss. No encoder in this term.
variables: soft-target InfoNCE + synthetic reconstruction, weight 0.1 + 1.0, delta target on real batches
runs.compared_to: Run 20 · Run 14 with the degradation direction as the target (delta target)
findings: Synthetic benchmark (known degradations on test HRs, no encoder): strong following, own target closest 51% (Run 20: 29%, chance 25%), low-pass PSNR to the exact target 39.8 dB (Run 20: 33.8); leak over signal 0.40 (Run 20: 0.73).
On real references the following does not improve: matched minus unmatched similarity 0.11 (Run 20: 0.11).

Real-data quality: LPIPS 0.0366 (Run 20: 0.0364), FID 41.2 (39.7). Diversity halves (0.008, Run 20: 0.016) and the outputs carry sharper speckled fine detail than the real LR: flat-region fine texture with panasonic_187 3.68 on seed 0 (Run 20: 3.22).
runs.verdict: Follows synthetic degradations well, but this does not transfer to real references and the outputs get an oversharp synthetic look.

runs.summary: As Run 9 (no degradation loss), plus the synthetic reconstruction term of Run 24. No encoder anywhere in the loss.
runs.purpose: Test whether synthetic pairs alone teach reference following, without the encoder-based loss.

runs.name: Run 26
runs.title: Run 20 + synthetic same-content pairs inside the degradation loss only
runs.summary: As Run 20, plus a second soft-target InfoNCE on the same synthetic pairs as Run 24: each output G(x, z, E(r_k)) is scored against J(y_k), the DEResNet embedding of the exact synthetic target. The target has the output's own content, so only the degradation can pick the answer. No pixel loss on the synthetic targets.
runs.purpose: Use synthetic pairs only in the degradation loss, keeping the image losses on real data.
variables: soft-target InfoNCE + synthetic InfoNCE, weight 0.1 + 0.1, delta target on real batches
runs.compared_to: Run 20 · Run 14 with the degradation direction as the target (delta target)
findings: Lowest leak of all runs: flat-region fine texture with panasonic_187 3.13 on seed 0 and 3.03 on seed 1 (Run 20: 3.22 / 3.35, Run 9 without degradation loss: 3.23); clean flat wall in the montage. Leak over signal on the synthetic benchmark 0.65 (Run 20: 0.73).
Reference following as Run 20: matched minus unmatched similarity 0.11, own in closest 2 67%.
Quality as Run 20 or slightly better: LPIPS 0.0357, FID 40.1 (Run 20: 0.0364, 39.7); diversity 0.015.
runs.verdict: Small but consistent gain over Run 20: less leak at equal following and quality. New best base.
